fullPassage:
(A) The manager of the Humane Society was out of town for two weeks, and Elaine was placed in charge. Since she had taken on this responsibility before, she was familiar with the challenges she might encounter — impounding stray animals, reuniting pets with their owners, informing people their pet hadn't been found, accepting animals from those who could no longer care for them, or turning animals away when the shelter was full. Though she found the work demanding, she handled these situations with confidence and calm.

(D) On the first day of the manager's absence, everything was running smoothly until a woman arrived with a cat and asked to leave it at the shelter. Elaine's first question was whether the cat was a stray or not, since the shelter was obligated to take in strays but could refuse owned pets. The woman said it was her cat and explained that she was moving and couldn't take it with her — a common excuse. Although the shelter sometimes accepted pets in such cases, it was already housing over ninety cats, nearly double its capacity of fifty, so Elaine had to politely refuse.

(C) Elaine calmly explained that there was no space available, but the woman became visibly upset and said, "If you don't take this cat, I'll just have to let it go somewhere." Although such statements were sadly not unusual, they always troubled Elaine. Still, she maintained professionalism, offered contact information for other shelters, and tried to help. The woman complained the alternatives were too far and repeated she had no other choice. Elaine then suggested the shelter might find a volunteer to transport the cat. In response, the woman, showing her frustration toward her, placed the cat's kennel in front of her, raised her voice, and left the shelter.

(B) Elaine could no longer hold it in. She gently put the cat in a kennel and brought it to the back isolation area. Then she went to the back room and called the absent manager, who encouraged her to let it all out. Elaine shared what happened and released her emotions while the manager listened. She felt much better afterward and was relieved to have someone she could talk to without fear of judgment. Since then, the manager has encouraged staff to come to her if they need to release emotions kept in at work — and she listens.

Elaine's first question was whether the cat was a stray or not, since the shelter was obligated to take in strays but could refuse owned pets. The woman said it was her cat and explained that she was moving and couldn't take it with her — a common excuse. Although the shelter sometimes accepted pets in such cases, it was already housing over ninety cats, nearly double its capacity of fifty, so Elaine had to __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 수용 능력의 두 배에 가까운 고양이를 이미 보호하고 있어 정중하게 거절해야 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ politely refuse: 정중하게 거절, 원문 일치 — 이미 정원 초과 상태
❌ ① gladly welcome: 기꺼이 환영, 정원 초과와 모순
❌ ② immediately call the manager: 매니저 부재 중
❌ ④ report the woman: 신고할 이유 없음
det.tip: 정원 50마리의 거의 두 배(90마리+) → 거절이 불가피한 상황

questions.passage: (C) Elaine calmly explained that there was no space available, but the woman became visibly upset and said, "If you don't take this cat, I'll just have to let it go somewhere." Although such statements were sadly not unusual, they always troubled Elaine. Still, she maintained (profession), offered contact information for other shelters, and tried to help.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하시오.

det.analysis: profession(직업/명사) → professionalism(전문성/직업정신/명사): maintained의 목적어로 추상명사 필요

questions.passage: (B) Elaine could no longer hold it in. She gently put the cat in a kennel and brought it to the back isolation area. Then she went to the back room and called the absent manager, who (encourage) her to let it all out.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하시오.

det.analysis: encourage(동사원형) → encouraged(과거형): 과거 시제 문맥(called, went 등)에 맞춤. who + 과거 동사.
det.tip: encourage → encouraged (과거형). 'the manager, who encouraged her' = 그녀를 격려한 매니저

questions.passage: (B) Elaine could no longer hold it in. She gently put the cat in a kennel and brought it to the back isolation area. Then she went to the back room and called the absent manager, who encouraged her to let it all out. Elaine shared what happened and released her emotions while the manager listened. She felt much better afterward and was relieved to have someone she could talk to __________. Since then, the manager has encouraged staff to come to her if they need to release emotions kept in at work — and she listens.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 비판에 대한 두려움 없이(without fear of judgment) 대화할 수 있는 사람이 있어 안도했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② without fear of judgment: 비판의 두려움 없이, 원문 일치 — 심리적 안전감
❌ ① with strict guidelines: 엄격한 지침과 함께, 반대 분위기
❌ ③ during business hours only: 근무 시간에만, 무관
❌ ④ about personal matters: 사적인 일에 대해, 맥락과 다름
det.tip: without fear of judgment — 비판/판단의 두려움 없이 마음을 열 수 있는 관계의 중요성

questions.passage:
(A) The manager of the Humane Society was out of town for two weeks, and Elaine was placed in charge. Since she had taken on this responsibility before, she was familiar with the challenges she might encounter — impounding stray animals, reuniting pets with their owners, informing people their pet hadn't been found, accepting animals from those who could no longer care for them, or turning animals away when the shelter was full. Though she found the work demanding, she handled these situations with confidence and calm.

(B) Elaine could no longer hold it in. She gently put the cat in a kennel and brought it to the back isolation area. Then she went to the back room and called the absent manager, who encouraged her to let it all out. Elaine shared what happened and released her emotions while the manager listened. She felt much better afterward. Since then, the manager has encouraged staff to come to her if they need to release emotions kept in at work — and she listens.
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용을 통해 알 수 있는 Elaine에 대한 설명으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: She was inexperienced in running the shelter.
She ignored the emotional impact of her work.
She coped with emotional strain by seeking support.
She refused to follow the shelter's policies.

det.korean: Elaine은 감정적 부담을 지지(support)를 구함으로써 극복했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ coped with emotional strain by seeking support: 매니저에게 전화해 감정을 풀어냄
❌ ① inexperienced: 경험 없는 — 이전에 책임을 맡은 적 있음(familiar)
❌ ② ignored emotional impact: 감정 무시 — 감정에 영향을 받았고 도움을 구함
❌ ④ refused to follow policies: 정책 거부 — 보호소 규정에 따라 거절함
det.tip: cope with(대처하다), emotional strain(감정적 부담), seek support(도움을 구하다)
